In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ZipA protein, which is a part of the septal assembly complex, plays a crucial role for the recruitment of DMinC/activator to the septal assembly.
the MinD/MinC complex has a high affinity for the septal ring, while the DicB/MinC complex is recruited to the septal ring through ZipA, and the MinC/ZipA/DicB complex inhibits division.
the MinC inhibitor must be present in both its cytoplasmic and membrane-associated forms to block division.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Min system is a highly dynamic system that has evolved multiple mechanisms for controlling FtsZ assembly.

MinD is required for the rapid pole-to- pole oscillation of MinD/MinC complexes that is essential for the accurate placement of the FtsZ ring, while DicB is required for the MinD-independent division block that is induced by the DMinC-DicB complex in MinC+ strains.
MinC is a division inhibitor that is recruited to FtsZ ring assemblies through a two-step process, which requires the MinD ATPase for efficient targeting.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the DMinC-DicB complex, like the DMinC-MinD complex, is targeted to septal rings by a mechanism that requires ZipA but not the other FtsZ-binding proteins.
ZipA is required to recruit DMinC/DiC to FtsZ assemblies and is therefore a critical component of the MinC-mediated division block.
the MinC inhibitor can be recruited to the septal ring by at least two distinct mechanisms, each of which is dependent upon a specific activator protein.
